title: Armstrong's 1931 benefit at the Army Base and Depression prices
summary: A 1931 Louisiana Weekly notice of Armstrong playing a hospital benefit prompts talk of prices and hard times after the 1929 bank closures.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Yeah, that was, yeah. That's about all it would have been.

Because you got to remember the banks had closed in 1929. Hardly anybody had any money in 30 and 31. And that's when you had tokens on the market. You don't remember the little tokens. No, I'm not. If you spent 15 cents or 25 cents, you had to come up with a token. Then they had this thing about half red beans and half rice, or either one-third meat, one-third beans, and one-third rice. So if you spent 50 cents, you could go home and cook yourself a dinner with half red beans, or one-third red beans, rice, and meat. You know, we have come through something in this state and in this country. This is really wild.
This is a...where's this from? I'm looking at this. That's out the Louisiana Weekly.
It's out the Weekly, okay. Out the Weekly, August 29, 1931.
This is of Louis Armstrong playing at... At Poland. He's playing for a hospital benefit. A benefit. A hospital work for colored at the U.S. Army Supply Base. Right. Which is at Poland and Dolphin.
Oh, Poland. And it's still there.
